_note: Golden set for the offline eval gate, grounded in the REAL document data/attention.pdf ('Attention Is All You Need', Vaswani et al., 2017). Every expected fact was read directly from the retrieved chunks of the built index (not from memory): h=8 heads and dk=dv=64 from p4::c1, d_model=512 from p4::c6, sine/cosine positional encodings from p5::c2-3, BLEU 28.4 EN-DE and 41.8 EN-FR from p0::c3 and p7::c3, Adam beta1=0.9 beta2=0.98 from p6::c7, WMT 2014 from p6::c4. The image golden targets Figure 2 (the attention diagrams) on page 3. Regenerate whenever the source document changes.

goldens.question: How many attention heads does the Transformer use, and what is the dimension of each head?
goldens.expected_output: The Transformer uses h = 8 parallel attention heads, and each head has dimension dk = dv = dmodel/h = 64.

goldens.question: How does the Transformer inject information about token position, given it has no recurrence or convolution?
goldens.expected_output: It adds positional encodings to the input embeddings, using sine and cosine functions of different frequencies, with the same dimension dmodel as the embeddings so the two can be summed.

goldens.question: What does Figure 2 in the paper illustrate about the attention mechanism?
goldens.expected_output: Figure 2 shows Scaled Dot-Product Attention on the left and Multi-Head Attention on the right, where multi-head attention runs several attention layers in parallel.

goldens.question: What BLEU scores does the Attention Is All You Need paper report for the big Transformer model on WMT 2014 English-to-German and English-to-French? Include the English-to-French discrepancy between the abstract/Table 2 and the body prose.
goldens.expected_output: The big Transformer achieved a BLEU score of 28.4 on WMT 2014 English-to-German. For English-to-French, the abstract/Table 2 reports 41.8, while the body prose reports 41.0.

goldens.question: Which optimizer and hyperparameters were used to train the models?
goldens.expected_output: The models were trained with the Adam optimizer using beta1 = 0.9, beta2 = 0.98, and epsilon = 10^-9, with a learning rate varied over the course of training.
